tool_analysis:
Step Analysis:
- The recorded browser session navigated to the Magento 1 admin Orders grid, analyzed the filter controls and grid structure, applied filters (order number, bill-to name, status), ran Search, Reset, used Select Visible and mass-action, triggered Export, and opened an Order View. Stable element hashes were recorded for the main interactive elements (order id input, bill-to input, status select, Search, Reset, Select Visible, massaction select/submit, export select/button, a View link).

Task Definition:
- Purpose: Provide a reusable, deterministic tool that performs a search on the Magento admin Orders grid using provided filter criteria and returns structured matching order rows. It also demonstrates mass-action and export interactions and can open a specific order view when requested.

Action Plan (detailed to-do list):
1. Navigate to the admin orders grid URL.
2. Populate all supported filter fields (increment_id, billing_name, date range, totals range, store, status) using stable selectors or recorded element hashes.
3. Click Search and wait for the grid to refresh.
4. Extract visible order rows into a structured list (increment id, internal id, purchased_on, bill_to, ship_to, grand_total, status, view_url).
5. Demonstrate mass-action: Select Visible, choose mass action, submit; wait for processing.
6. Demonstrate export: choose format and click export to trigger download.
7. Navigate to Order View for a provided internal order_id and extract order-level details.

Variable Identification (inputs):
- increment_id (filter name increment_id)
- billing_name (billing_name)
- created_at_from, created_at_to (created_at[from]/created_at[to])
- status (visible option text from Status select)
- store_id (visible text for store select name 'store_id')
- base_grand_total_from/to and grand_total_from/to (numeric/text range inputs)
- export_format (CSV/Excel XML/XML visible option text)
- mass_action (visible option text from massaction select)
- view_order_id (internal order_id used in order view URL)
- base_url (admin base URL to build navigation targets)

Step Optimization and Determinism:
- Use recorded elementHash values where available for the most deterministic interactions (these were captured during the session: order id input, bill-to input, status select, Search button, Select Visible, massaction select/submit, export select/button, View link). For elements without an elementHash (date inputs, totals inputs, store select) the tool uses id/name-based CSS selectors that follow Magento conventions (e.g. input[name='created_at[from]'], select[name='store_id']).
- Navigation to the orders grid uses a direct URL rather than clicking through the admin menu (more reliable).
- Extraction uses a single extract_page_content step to return structured order rows; the extraction goal specifies which fields to capture so the implementation can reliably parse the grid rows and href patterns (/sales_order/view/order_id/).
- The tool is sequential and deterministic (no branching). All inputs are parameterized; if a parameter is empty the tool will input an empty string or attempt to select the given text (caller must supply appropriate visible text for selects).

Selectors and Stability Notes:
- Prefer scoping to #sales_order_grid as recorded. The tool uses elementHashes for elements that were interacted with during recording. For other controls, selectors adhere to Magento 1 core naming conventions.
- Mass-action and export flows may trigger downloads or server-side actions; the tool waits briefly after those steps to let navigation/AJAX begin. Confirm behavior in the target environment.

Caveats and Recommendations:
- The tool assumes the agent is already authenticated as the admin user (session present). Do not include login steps in this tool.
- Some select_change steps require exact visible option text; callers must provide the visible option label as seen in the admin UI (e.g. 'Complete', 'CSV', 'Print All').
- Because the tool is intentionally sequential and non-branching, supplying empty or invalid values for select fields may cause the recorded selectors to attempt an invalid selection. Test with real values first.
- For opening a specific Order View it is more reliable to navigate directly to the order view URL (used here) than to click the per-row View link (which requires locating the exact row link). The recorded URL pattern /sales_order/view/order_id/<id>/ is applied.

This tool implements the recorded browser actions in a deterministic, parameterized sequence suitable for re-execution against the same Magento admin interface.
name: magento_find_orders_tool
description: Search the Magento 1 admin Orders grid using provided filter criteria, extract matching order rows, and (optionally) perform mass-action, export, and open a specific Order View. Uses recorded stable selectors and element hashes from a Magento 1.9.3.8 demo admin instance.

steps.description: Navigate to the Magento Admin Orders grid. If base_url is empty this resolves to '/sales_order/' on the recorded host.
Wait briefly for the grid and JS to initialize.
Enter the Order # into the increment_id filter (scoped to recorded element hash).
Enter Bill to Name into the billing_name filter (scoped to recorded element hash).
Set Purchased On - From date (if provided). Uses the canonical filter name 'created_at[from]'.
Set Purchased On - To date (if provided). Uses the canonical filter name 'created_at[to]'.
Set G.T. (Base) From value (numeric/text).
Set G.T. (Base) To value (numeric/text).
Set G.T. (Purchased) From value (numeric/text).
Set G.T. (Purchased) To value (numeric/text).
Select the Status option using the recorded Status select element hash. Provide visible option text (e.g. 'Complete').
Select Store view (if provided). Uses select[name='store_id'] under the grid scope.
Click the Search button (recorded element hash) to apply the filters.
Wait for the grid to refresh after applying filters.
Read the updated Orders grid and return structured records for matching orders.
steps.goal: Extract order rows: for each visible row capture increment_id (display), internal order_id (from href if available), purchased_on, bill_to_name, ship_to_name, grand_total, status, and view_url.

steps.description: Click 'Select Visible' to check all visible row checkboxes (recorded element hash).
Choose the mass-action option (recorded massaction select element hash). Provide visible action text exactly (e.g. 'Print All').
Click mass-action Submit (recorded element hash) to apply the chosen mass action to selected rows.
Wait for any mass-action processing or downloads to start/complete (AJAX or navigation).
Choose Export format from the Export dropdown (recorded export select element hash). Provide visible text such as 'CSV'.
Click the Export/Export button (recorded element hash) to trigger the export/download.
Wait for export/download navigation to begin.
Navigate to the Order View for the provided internal order_id (if view_order_id supplied). Uses the recorded admin URL pattern.
Read and return key Order View information for the opened order.
steps.goal: Extract key fields from the Order View page: summary (order date, status), billing/shipping addresses, items ordered (product, sku, qty, price, row total), and order totals.

input_schema.name: increment_id
input_schema.description: Order increment id (Order #). Matches input[name='increment_id'] in the grid filter. Leave empty for no order id filter.

input_schema.name: billing_name
input_schema.description: Bill to Name free-text filter. Matches input[name='billing_name'] in the grid filter.

input_schema.name: created_at_from
input_schema.description: Purchased On - From date. Use format MM/DD/YYYY or the admin locale's date format. Maps to input[name='created_at[from]'].

input_schema.name: created_at_to
input_schema.description: Purchased On - To date. Use format MM/DD/YYYY or the admin locale's date format. Maps to input[name='created_at[to]'].

input_schema.name: status
input_schema.description: Order status visible option text (e.g. 'Complete', 'Pending'). Will be selected in the Status dropdown. Leave empty to keep current selection.

input_schema.name: store_id
input_schema.description: Store view visible text to select (e.g. 'Main Website'). Maps to select[name='store_id'] in the grid filter. Leave empty to keep current selection.

input_schema.name: base_grand_total_from
input_schema.description: G.T. (Base) From - numeric/text value. Maps to input[name='base_grand_total[from]'].

input_schema.name: base_grand_total_to
input_schema.description: G.T. (Base) To - numeric/text value. Maps to input[name='base_grand_total[to]'].

input_schema.name: grand_total_from
input_schema.description: G.T. (Purchased) From - numeric/text value. Maps to input[name='grand_total[from]'].

input_schema.name: grand_total_to
input_schema.description: G.T. (Purchased) To - numeric/text value. Maps to input[name='grand_total[to]'].

input_schema.name: export_format
input_schema.description: Export format visible option text to select in the Export selector (e.g. 'CSV', 'Excel XML', 'XML'). If provided, the tool will attempt to trigger Export after performing the search.

input_schema.name: mass_action
input_schema.description: Mass action visible option text to select (e.g. 'Print All', 'Cancel'). The tool will (after selecting visible rows) choose this action and submit mass-action.

input_schema.name: view_order_id
input_schema.description: Order internal id (not increment id) to open in the Order View (the controller URL uses order_id). Example: '204'. If provided, the tool will navigate to the Order View URL after the grid actions.

input_schema.name: base_url
input_schema.description: Base admin URL to use for navigation. Example: 'http://dockerized-magento.local/index.php/admin'. If omitted the recorded admin path 'http://dockerized-magento.local/index.php/admin/sales_order/' is used for navigation.
